question: When fats and oils are oxidised, they develop a smell and taste that is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**rancid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When **fats and oils** are exposed to air, they undergo a chemical reaction known as **oxidation**. This process results in the development of a foul smell and an unpleasant taste, a condition commonly referred to as **rancidity**.
 
• The primary cause of this phenomenon is the **oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids** present in the food. During this reaction, oxygen molecules attack the **double bonds** of the fatty acid chains.
 
• This chemical breakdown leads to the formation of highly volatile substances, including **aldehydes**, **ketones**, and **short-chain carboxylic acids**, which provide the characteristic "off" flavor and pungent odor.
